result.reason: Section 2.1 facially adopts the fallback: a current 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days’ notice, with a shortfall true-up rather than a penalty. The change is confined to the relevant commitment language. However, it is not coherently integrated with Sections 9.4 and 12.3: Section 9.4 says Customer owes only for Services provided through termination, while Section 12.3 states there is no minimum-volume commitment. The amendment also does not specify how or when a reduction or true-up is calculated. These conflicts risk altering or obscuring the existing convenience-termination economics, so unrelated commercial intent is not reliably preserved and drafting quality is weak.
